data: Is the red line always higher than the green line throughout the figure?

The red line represents the percentage of types covered, while the green line represents the percentage of sentences covered. The caption provides numerical data about the distribution of types and sentences based on their frequency. The red line starts at approximately 100% for the lowest threshold type frequency and decreases sharply as the threshold increases. The green line also starts at approximately 100% but decreases more gradually compared to the red line. Both lines show a downward trend as the threshold increases. The caption states that the vast majority of types (80%) are rare (have less than 10 occurrences), which aligns with the steep decline of the red line. The red line is consistently above the green line throughout the figure, indicating that the percentage of types covered is always higher than the percentage of sentences covered. Therefore, the answer is yes, the red line is always higher than the green line throughout the figure.
